subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: Should OpenClaw expose Telegram custom emoji through raw/rich HTML only, through Telegram entity arrays, or through a shared Markdown/IR custom-emoji span that the Telegram plugin turns into Telegram payloads?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but solving it expands a public message-tool/plugin contract and affects delivery fallback behavior across several Telegram funnels.

options.title: Design typed entity/IR contract
options.body: Pick a typed representation that can round-trip custom emoji IDs through sends, edits, captions, and replies while preserving the current HTML fallback behavior.

options.title: Keep raw/rich HTML only
options.body: Document the current `<tg-emoji>` and `richMessages` path as the supported surface and explicitly decline first-class entity arrays for now.

options.title: Add Telegram-only entity fields
options.body: Expose `entities` and `caption_entities` only through Telegram-owned action/channelData surfaces without changing shared Markdown IR yet.

recommendation.title: Design typed entity/IR contract
recommendation.body: Pick a typed representation that can round-trip custom emoji IDs through sends, edits, captions, and replies while preserving the current HTML fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest signal from the prior review on this exact issue and relevant Telegram formatting/API history.
